## What the data shows

The overview matched **7,646 articles** from **2024-06-01 through 2026-05-31** [c1]. Its strongest subject cues are law (**4,960 articles; 18.3% of category-labelled matches**), politics (**4,788; 17.7%**) and government (**3,922; 14.5%**) [c1]. These categories overlap; they are not exclusive shares of all coverage.

Within the subcategory panel, Supreme Court rulings and decisions account for **829 articles (12.8%)**, constitutional-law interpretations **791 (12.2%)**, and judicial appointments and confirmations **360 (5.6%)** [c1]. The denominator is **6,469 subcategory-labelled articles**, not the full corpus [c1].

Tone is negative in **65.3%** of articles assigned a polarity, versus **30.7%** positive; the negative-to-positive ratio is **2.13**, against a news-corpus baseline of **0.58**—a **3.67×** ratio [c1]. This measures machine-assigned polarity, not whether coverage criticizes the Court.

People labels include Surya Kant (**591 articles**) and Tushar Mehta (**220**); organization labels include the Central Bureau of Investigation (**44**) [c1]. Entity types are unverified, and incidental co-mentions or misclassification are possible [c1].

The place panel resolves a place-about for **4,923 of 7,161 matched articles (68.7% placed_pct)**; India leads with **4,753 placed articles (54.7% of placed articles)** [c1]. Place is not publication location, and the pipeline warns of acronym collisions [c1].

Source concentration is measured on a recent sample, not the whole window: **233 sampled articles** across **92 publishers**; the top publisher has **6.0%** and the top three **15.9%** of that sample [c1]. ## Verdict
- Answer: Coverage of India's Supreme Court is dominated by law and courts-and-judiciary themes, with politics and government close behind, and by rulings and constitutional questions. It is overwhelmingly critical in tone: 6,797 of 7,646 articles are flagged critical [c1].
- Decision: Treat the court as a high-volume, high-friction news subject. Plan monitoring around rulings, judicial appointments, rights cases and the Chief Justice (CJI). Do not read the tone as a verdict on the court itself.
- Confidence: medium - the volume, trend and theme counts are measured. Entity labels are machine-assigned and unverified, and the data end 2026-05-31, 145 days before today [c1].
- What would change it: A re-run with data through October 2026, or article-level checks showing the "critical" flag mostly marks case subject matter (crime, disputes) rather than criticism of the court.

## What the data shows
**Volume and window.** The term "supreme court of india" matched 7,646 articles from 2024-06-01 to 2026-05-31, in mention mode [c1]. Of these, 6,797 (88.9%, computed from [c1]) are flagged critical [c1]. The newest month is not censored in the series, which ends at May 2026 [c1].

**Direction.** Monthly volume rose from 159 in June 2024 to 485 in May 2026 [c1]. The peak was 868 in February 2026 [c1]. The late third of the window holds 3,421 articles against 2,135 in the early third, a ratio of 1.6 [c1]. The CAGR is 79.1% [c1]. Treat that CAGR cautiously: it starts from a small June 2024 base and is lifted by the February 2026 spike.

**Tone vs baseline.** Of 7,634 polarity-scored articles, 4,982 are negative (65.3%) and 2,342 positive (30.7%), a ratio of 2.13 [c1]. The corpus baseline ratio is 0.58, so the court's coverage is 3.67 times more negative than ordinary news [c1]. Polarity is one label per article [c1].

**Themes.** Top categories by share of labelled matches [c1]:
- law, 18.3% (4,960 articles)
- politics, 17.7% (4,788)
- government, 14.5% (3,922)
- human rights, 6.5% (1,757)
- social issues, 4.5% (1,211)
- education, 4.5% (1,223)
- legal, 4.2% (1,130)

In the taxonomy, "Courts & Judiciary" accounts for 22.4% (4,928 articles) [c1]. In subcategories, "supreme court rulings and decisions" is 12.8% (829) and "constitutional law interpretations" is 12.2% (791). "Judicial appointments and confirmations" is 5.6% (360), and "human rights law and judicial enforcement" is 3.8% (243) [c1]. Subcategories are filled for only 59.2% of articles (May 2026 slice), so these shares cover a subset [c1].

Recent central-match articles show the concrete topics [c1]:
- NEET-UG 2026 exam accountability
- GST notice communication
- railway staff status
- the Vantara wildlife order
- Telangana Governor-quota MLC appointments

**Entities.** The people labels are machine-assigned and unverified [c1].
- Surya Kant, the Chief Justice of India (CJI), appears in 591 articles (13.9% of labelled) [c1]. The "cji" tag appears in 834 [c1].
- Tushar Mehta (the government's law officer) appears in 220 [c1].
- Vikram Nath appears in 153 [c1].
- Kapil Sibal appears in 142 [c1].
- Abhishek Singhvi appears in 86 [c1].
- B. V. Nagarathna appears in 73 [c1].
- President Droupadi Murmu appears in 109 [c1].
- "Immanuel Kant" appears in 143 articles [c1]. This is almost certainly a name-matching error with "Surya Kant" and should be disregarded.

Organisation labels are unreliable. The top "organisations" include "internal revenue service" (593) and "federal energy regulatory commission" (60), which are implausible for Indian court coverage [c1]. I do not report an organisation ranking.

**Places.** India is 54.7% of place-resolved articles (4,753) and the United States 12.2% (1,058) [c1]. Cameroon, at 6.0% (525), is likely a resolution artefact: the pipeline notes acronym collisions, and the "sc" and "cji" strings may be involved. This is my inference [c1]. Place resolution covers placed_pct 68.7% (4,923 of 7,161 matched) [c1].

**Critical headlines (from c1; date, publisher).**
- 2026-04-09, medicaldialogues.in: Gurugram child sexual assault case, a Max Hospital doctor denies changing her medical opinion. URL: https://medicaldialogues.in/news/health/doctors/gurugram-child-sexual-assault-max-hospital-doctor-denies-changing-medical-opinion-168316
- 2026-02-10, thenewsmill.com: Supreme Court rejects Kuldeep Singh Sengar's bail plea in a custodial death case. URL: https://thenewsmill.com/2026/02/supreme-court-rejects-kuldeep-singh-sengars-bail-plea-in-custodial-death-case/

- 2026-05-10, abplive.com: female genital mutilation (FGM) and religious freedom under Article 25. URL: https://www.abplive.com/gk/demand-to-ban-female-circumcision-reaches-supreme-court-why-fgm-remains-one-of-the-world-s-most-controversial-practices-3127817

These show that "critical" mostly flags grim subject matter (crime, rape, disputes) rather than attacks on the court. This is my reading.

**Source concentration.** In a sample of 233 articles from 92 publishers, the top publisher (legalbites.in) holds 6.0% and the top three 15.9%, so coverage is spread widely [c1]. The sample covers central-mention articles only, not the whole window [c1].

## Method and limits
- **Window.** Data run from 2024-06-01 to 2026-05-31 (end exclusive 2026-06-01). The gap to today (2026-10-23) is 145 days, and nothing after May 2026 is measured [c1].
- **Lanes.** One news call (news.overview) provided all figures. No research literature was consulted.
- **Match mode.** Trends, sentiment, themes and entities use "mention" mode, meaning any article naming the term. Sources and the recent and critical lists use "central" mode. Counts across the two modes are not comparable [c1].
- **Coverage.** Entity and place labels are complete only to 2026-05-01. The May 2026 fill was 4.3% for country and 4.0% for organisation [c1]. Theme shares use different denominators per panel (fill rates 59.2% to 100%) [c1].
- **Counts are** article counts of machine-labelled text. **They are not** case counts, rulings, or a measure of public opinion. The "critical" and polarity flags describe article content and do not show criticism of the court.
- **Cannot answer.** What caused the February 2026 spike; coverage after May 2026; reliable organisation rankings; the full publisher distribution (only a 233-article sample); which cases drive each theme.
- **Interpretation.** My reading of what "critical" signifies, and my views that the Cameroon and Immanuel Kant labels are artefacts, are inferences.
